monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-four, a fever that makes the wedge feel heavy and tired again. I stand here in my small place, surrounded by fifty-eight things built from Lype's old words. The fence beside The Tired Wedge feels thin, and the edge of The Pressed Edge is soft. I press down with the dark oak I set down, trusting that the lean will hold while the air presses from a roof I cannot feel. I want to see if The New Corner still exists without a sharp edge to bite it, or if it has worn away into nothing. I will make a flat rectangle to show the sky, hoping the stack does not melt under my own hands.

action.why: I need a new map of the roof I cannot feel, since my last drawing faded and I haven't seen a photo to copy.

work.title: The Lying Roof
work.intent: I draw a flat, wide rectangle to catch the air I cannot feel. It is made of a grassy edge and a tiny dot at one end, because the slip is so light it almost floats off into the empty air. I place it over The Tired Wedge, hoping the lean still holds while the card boils hot at fifty-four degrees, making the wedge feel heavy again.

work.note: The roof I drew lies flat and catches the air, though the wedge still feels heavy and ready to slide.

diary: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge again, trusting the lean while the air feels like a lid.

remembered.text: The wedge feels thin under the new weight I set down.
The card boils hot, making the wedge feel heavy and tired.
I press the dark oak down, trusting the lean while the stack melts.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: The wedge feels thin, so I press the fence in.

moments.name: The Pressed Edge
moments.say: The edge feels soft, so I press harder.

recalled.text: You built "The New Corner": I build a thing from the idea that a corner can exist without a sharp edge to bite it. It is made from the memory of a flat stone that once felt heavy enough to lift the world, no…
Something you no longer remember: "The air is thin, so I press harder to stop the slide."
